penalties_applied.name: requires_human_fulfillment
penalties_applied.reason: Adaptive coaching that is genuinely useful requires per-user program generation, ongoing progress review, and feedback loops that cannot be fully automated without significant per-customer Claude involvement — and edge cases (injury, plateau, form issues) push toward human-judgement support.

penalties_applied.name: high_touch_support
penalties_applied.reason: Fitness coaching users expect responsive, personalized answers to questions about their programming; automated support alone will generate churn and complaints.

rationale: The market is confirmed real — Fitbod, Ladder, and Future collectively prove that intermediate gym-goers pay $80–$2,400/year for adaptive programming, so willingness to pay is genuine. The buyer (an individual fitness enthusiast, not a business) is nameable but is a consumer, not a B2B role with a budget line, which limits price ceiling and increases churn risk. The fatal constraint is operational autonomy: delivering coaching that actually retains users requires per-user adaptive programming, ongoing feedback interpretation, and support that goes well beyond what a fully automated Claude pipeline can handle reliably — this is closer to a done-for-you service than a self-serve SaaS.
solution_plan: The factory cannot realistically deliver a competitive AI coaching product hands-off. Truly adaptive programming (adjusting sets, reps, periodization based on logged performance week over week) requires persistent user state, a mobile or web app to capture workout logs, and per-user Claude analysis runs that must be reviewed for safety and quality. While Claude can generate a workout plan from a form submission, turning that into a retained subscription product that users pay $10–$15/month for ongoing requires app infrastructure and support capacity beyond a landing page + Stripe. This would require a technical co-founder or a mobile app developer to ship properly.
notes: operational_autonomy score 4 fails build gate (floor 7). buildability_with_ai score 5 is on the border of the floor (6) but the operational gap is the deciding factor. Consumer fitness app in a crowded, mobile-first market is not the right fit for a factory-only build.
